details:
Issue: Often I see people mass unfriend others. Or you get removed during a purge after a break. In a real social setting you don't go out of your way to prevent yourself from seeing old friends. However in VRC to maintain orderly lists people clean up often. I think its absurd the only options are embracing the clutter, or removing any realistic chances of finding that person again. 

Solution: A system that tracks inactive users and automaticaly moves them into an archive group, hiding them from your main list. 

Details: For this to be done correctly ideally it would have a drop down menu letting you select from a couple of preset timeframes when to move someone into the archive. You should be able to manually archive and unarchive friends at will. You should also be able to exclude a certain friend group from being archived if you wish. VRC already keeps track of how long users have been offline, so that would be fairly easy to handle, but if you wanted to invest a bit more resources to the feature you could have it be based on how long since you have been in a world with that user. You could also have an easy one click clear archive button and confirm to make clearing it out easy for those who want to. I believe instead of showing as a friend in an instance they should have an archived user indicator for all those moments you run into someone with the "who in the world is that" issue. 

How this helps: By hiding these archived friends from the main friend list you retain a sense of order without the classic burning of the bridges people do. Yet at the same time everyone would still be at your fingertips with minimal effort, making finding old friends, reliably easy. (incase of name changes or such). All in all, just because someone goes inactive, doesnt mean the connection should be over for good.
title: Friend Archive System
